title: Changing the Subject of a Formula Flashcards

cards.front: What defines the subject of a formula?
cards.back: The variable written on its own, usually on the left-hand side.

options.text: The variable written on its own, usually on the left-hand side.
options.explanation: The subject is the variable isolated on one side of the formula. By convention, it is usually written alone on the left-hand side.

options.text: The variable written most often, usually on the right-hand side.
options.explanation: Frequency does not determine the subject, and variables on the right usually form the expression. The subject is the variable written on its own, usually on the left.

options.text: The variable with the highest power, usually on the left-hand side.
options.explanation: The highest power matters when identifying a polynomial’s degree, not its subject. The subject is whichever variable has been isolated on its own, usually on the left.

options.text: The variable being multiplied, usually on the right-hand side.
options.explanation: Being part of a multiplication does not make a variable the subject. The subject must be isolated on its own and is usually placed on the left-hand side.
